page: Amazon Web Services i3en.3xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 6-core, 12-thread Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 35 MB of L3 cache, support for AVX-512 vector instructions, and 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance incorporates 7,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and maintains a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark evaluations characterize the i3en.3xlarge by strong storage capacity alongside moderate compute throughput. Single-threaded benchmarks report lower-tier performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1034.0 and gzip compression reaching 21.91 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics settle within median ranges, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 5296.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 11204.43. Memory throughput measures 71.38 GB/sec for uncached read blocks and 45.05 GB/sec for writes. In application-level tests, the server delivered 9.96 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 9.21 GB/sec in static web serving, while showing limited capability for medium-sized LLM inference workloads.

The instance profile balances significant local NVMe storage and high memory density against conservative per-core processing speeds. It delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for architectures needing massive low-latency local disk space paired with substantial memory per thread, eliminating the overhead of dedicated network storage volumes. Best-fit workloads include distributed NoSQL databases, transactional databases, search indexing engines, log analytics clusters, and data warehousing systems requiring immediate access to dense local NVMe storage.
description: Amazon Web Services i3en.3xlarge is a storage-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs running at 3.1 GHz, paired with 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory and 7,500 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. The platform provides a 12 Gbps baseline network capacity without GPU acceleration. Benchmark results indicate moderate multi-core processing performance, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 5296.0 and 9.96 million Redis SET operations per second, counterbalanced by modest single-thread metrics such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1034.0. With an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio and high local storage density, this configuration provides a balanced environment for I/O-intensive workloads, including transactional and NoSQL databases, search clusters, and high-throughput log processing systems.
